circumstances: The researcher closes out the partial replication and begins a deliberate transition toward the next project. They write a short internal replication report, archive the exact configurations and outputs, and compare several possible directions. One idea about subgroup-specific calibration initially looks promising, but a literature search reveals that the basic framing is already well studied. A different question about calibration under changing class prevalence remains less settled and appears feasible with existing code. The researcher does not start a new experiment; instead, they narrow the question and define a small literature-reading task for the next day. There is also routine repository maintenance and a brief unrelated browsing detour.

activities.title: Close and archive the replication study
activities.summary: The researcher wrote an internal replication report, summarized the partial reproduction and unresolved evaluation ambiguity, checked repository state, and committed the replication documentation and configuration.
activities.context: The bounded replication reached its stopping rule on Day 20.

activities.title: Evaluate candidate next research questions
activities.summary: The researcher compared several possible directions. Subgroup-specific calibration appeared initially promising but recent literature made the basic framing less novel. Attention shifted toward calibration under changing class prevalence, where existing work left a narrower question worth investigating.
activities.context: Post-submission transition after closing the replication.

activities.title: Research ideas and incidental browsing
activities.summary: A short unrelated product-browsing detour occurred before the researcher returned to the ideas document and listed candidate datasets and unresolved questions without starting implementation.

activities.title: Narrow the next research question
activities.summary: The researcher refined the class-prevalence calibration question, wrote a small literature task for the next day, watched part of an unrelated conference talk, and then finalized a short reading list while parking other ideas.
activities.context: Transition from broad idea generation to a deliberately small next step.

key_observations: The replication was formally documented and archived rather than left as an ambiguous open loop.
The first candidate next direction, subgroup-specific calibration, lost novelty after checking recent literature.
A narrower question about calibration when class prevalence changes emerged as more promising and feasible with existing infrastructure.
The researcher deliberately stopped at a literature task rather than beginning a new experiment before the question was sufficiently specified.
Some unrelated browsing and a conference talk occurred, but neither became part of the research plan.
priority_alignment: The replication closure was completed before substantial new project exploration began.
The main planning effort was spent comparing research questions rather than immediately coding.
The next step is intentionally limited to literature synthesis and question refinement.
important_uncertainty: It is not yet clear whether the class-prevalence direction contains a sufficiently distinct contribution.
The appropriate datasets and evaluation setup for the new question have not been selected.
The parked ideas may become relevant later, so deprioritized does not mean permanently abandoned.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Read the short set of papers on calibration under changing class prevalence, identify the exact unresolved assumption or evaluation gap, and decide whether it warrants a small pilot.

primary_action.title: Validate the new research question
primary_action.reason: The replication is closed and one candidate direction has emerged, but its novelty and experimental scope are not established yet.

secondary_action.title: Keep implementation paused
secondary_action.reason: Starting a new experiment before the literature gap and evaluation setup are clear would recreate the exploratory expansion the researcher just avoided in the replication study.

things_not_to_do: Do not begin coding the new calibration experiment before reviewing the relevant literature.
Do not revive subgroup calibration merely because it is easy to implement.
Do not reopen the completed replication unless new evidence changes the documented stopping decision.
Do not turn the candidate dataset list into a broad benchmark project yet.
